title: Build, Ship, Shape: Amazon Developer Hackathon
description: <html> <head></head> <body></body> </html> Welcome to the Amazon Developer Hackathon For the first time, Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all part of one global hackathon. Build for one product or use several to connect the living room, the front door, and the cloud. Get started now with our SDKs, simulators, and sample code. New to building for Amazon devices and services? We'll help you get from idea to submission with documentation and live office hours. Use our AI tools to prototype and troubleshoot along the way. Choose a track and show off what you build! 🚀 Why join? Be part of the first hackathon where Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee are all open to outside developers at once Your product feedback goes directly to the teams building Fire TV, Alexa+, Ring, and Bee Compete for a share of $190K value of cash and AWS credits, plus a 1:1 meeting with the Amazon Developer team for track winners Get Started Pick your track: Fire TV, Alexa+, Bee, or Ring Set up the developer environment for your track (see Resources ) Review the track details and requirements to start building Submit your working demo, code repo, and product feedback by the deadline

title: Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon
description: Welcome to the Nebius x NVIDIA Global AI Hackathon Build a working AI system on open, independent infrastructure, and own the whole thing. The NVIDIA x Nebius Global AI Hackathon is for AI builders, ML engineers, founders, and anyone shipping practical, high-performance AI. You'll build with NVIDIA open source models served on Nebius through Nebius Token Factory, on high performance GPU infrastructure. Experiment with new ideas, push the boundaries of open source AI, and submit a project for a chance to win prizes and recognition. Join fellow builders for technical onboarding, casual workshops, team formation, focused build time, and feedback as you participate in the Global AI Hackathon. Find your nearby city/event here !

title: PayPal AI Hackathon
description: About the challenge PayPal already moves money for millions of people and businesses, every day, all over the world. This hackathon is us opening that platform up and asking what happens when you put AI behind the wheel. New agents, new ways to pay and get paid, tools nobody's built yet. We want to see what you make of it. AI is changing how people build, buy, sell, work, connect, and move money. Now it's your turn to imagine what comes next. Build What's Next with PayPal and AI is a global online hackathon inviting developers, designers, founders, students, and builders to create something new using PayPal and AI . There are no prescribed problem statements and no set of tracks. Build an agent, an app, an automation, a new payment experience, a business tool, a social product, or something we haven't thought of yet. The only fundamental requirement: your project must meaningfully use both PayPal and AI . Why Join? Build something ambitious — Turn an idea into a working project using PayPal and AI. Explore what’s next — Experiment with new ways people, businesses, and AI agents can interact with money and payments. Win part of $ 69,750 in total prizes — Compete for overall prizes and special awards across creativity, impact, execution, and more. Show what you can build — Put your project in front of PayPal judges, developers, and the wider hackathon community. Learn by building — Explore PayPal APIs, AI tools, agents, automations, and emerging development workflows. Build your way — Join individually or as a team, and start something new or meaningfully advance an existing project. Get started Get a PayPal Developer account (5 minutes) Review example projects and brainstorm your own (30 minutes) Webinars Oct 6th 9am PT - 9:45am PT ~ Start building with PayPal Oct 7th 9am PT - 9:30am PT ~ Power Your PayPal Hackathon Project with APIMatic Context Plugins Oct 12th 7am PT - 7:45am PT ~ Build a payments dashboard without building a dashboard Oct 13th 1am PT - 2am PT ~ Start building with PayPal

title: OpenCV AI Competition 2026, powered by AWS
description: About The Competition • Competition launch, registration, and proposal submission—runs August 12- 2026; proposals are accepted starting August 13. • 50 teams will be selected to receive a cloud compute grant valued at $150. All other teams, including those that submit the cloud compute grant proposal remain eligible to continue to the two-month build phase. Apply for your grant here. • Final projects are due October 26, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. • Every entry must use OpenCV 5 for substantive image or video analysis and run a meaningful component on AWS. • Two optional featured paths offer separate $1,000 awards: the Best Use of COOL Award and the Agentic Vision Award. Sponsor: Amazon Web Services (“Amazon” or “Sponsor”) Administrator: OpenCV Foundation (OpenCV or Administrator, and together with Amazon, the “organizers”) Join, Build, and Win Turn an ambitious idea into a working vision application, demonstrate measurable value, and share it with the global OpenCV community. The competition emphasizes Physical AI and Generative AI systems in which visual understanding drives useful decisions, actions, predictions, or interactions. Entries may pursue either featured path below, combine both, or take another approach and remain fully eligible to win a prize.. Projects may use any programming language or supporting hardware, provided they meet the core OpenCV 5 and AWS requirements on this page. Build Phase — Two Months From August 26 through October 26, teams will build, evaluate, document, and submit their final projects. • Teams are encouraged to join the official Slack channel to collaborate with others, and to use the #OpenCVComp26 hashtag on social media to share progress and milestones. • Teams who received a cloud compute grant must complete one 30-minute Zoom check-in with an organizing committee member during October 7-14 to receive the other 50% of their grant. • Teams must maintain active development and provide a concise progress update at the check-in. • Final submissions are due on October 26 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time. Final Judging and Winners Final judging will take place from October 27 through November 9. Winners are scheduled to be announced on November 10 during an OpenCV Live! webinar or another announced OpenCV channel. What AWS Grant Proposals Must Include Each proposal must include: A team name A clear problem statement and intended real-world impact. The planned OpenCV 5 image or video analysis. The planned AWS architecture and services. A high-level architecture diagram or technical description. The target users or beneficiaries. The proposed evaluation method and judge demonstration. Whether the team intends to pursue the COOL path, the Agentic Vision path, both, or neither. Team Bio: A short team bio of all team members and their participation in any hackathons or competitions. Team strength will be used to judge the recipients of the cloud compute grant. Apply For an AWS Compute Grant Here Free AWS Credits for New Members New AWS customers are eligible to receive $100 in AWS Free Tier credits when they sign up for a Free Plan account and may earn up to $100 more through eligible activities. Teams may use these credits for eligible AWS services in this competition, subject to current AWS Free Tier terms , service availability, and expiration rules. Use of the Free Tier Credits is subject to the AWS Promotional Credit Terms & Conditions . AWS Promotional Credits are not redeemable for cash and can only be applied to AWS Services.

title: Build With AI: Basics
description: <html> <head></head> <body></body> </html> Build With AI: Basics Build a working first draft of an app in an afternoon using AI best practices, with a set of reusable skills in your coding agent. Learn with a live build session, office hours, community, and a $2,500 prize pool, while creating something useful to your work or your life. About the challenge Devpost has launched a new kind of hackathon: shorter, built around learning, and open to join every month. Have you ever asked an AI to help you code something, only to watch it repeat a mistake you already fixed, forget a decision you made ten prompts ago, or hand back code that "works" but you can't explain? It happens to almost everyone who starts building with AI. Nobody showed you the basics. This hackathon does. You'll build a proof of concept: a small app that runs and does one thing end to end. To get there, you'll install the Devpost Learn Skill Pack , step-by-step guides that live inside your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or any agent that supports skills). The skills interview you about your idea, help you plan it before any code gets written, build it with you, and get it ready to submit. You'll finish with a running app, the plan that got you there, and a habit you can reuse on every project after this one. Why join Learn to plan before you build, by letting the AI interview you. It's the habit that keeps AI-built projects from turning into a mess. Try skills in your coding agent: reusable, step-by-step guides that work across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and others. Get help from real people: a live build session, office hours, and a live project review. Win a share of $2,500. First place takes $1,250 plus a feature in the Devpost newsletter and on Devpost's socials. Everyone who submits an eligible project gets a Devpost Learn badge. Get started You'll need Node.js and Git installed, a coding agent that supports skills, and an empty folder for your project. In your empty project folder, run npx skills add challengepost/learn-ai-basics --all -y Open your coding agent in that folder and say "run 1-start." It takes it from there. Join the Devpost Discord for questions, office hours, and other builders' projects. Register for the Live Build Session , Thursday, Oct 1 at 1:00 pm ET, where we run the whole process start to finish. Recorded if you can't make it. RSVP for Cup of Joe office hours: Tuesday, Oct 6 and Tuesday, Oct 13 , 3:00 pm ET, in Discord voice. Bring your project and your questions, and get live feedback from Joe and other builders. Just drop in, no Zoom needed. Register for Will It Ship , Thursday, Oct 22 at 3:00 pm ET. A live review of about five submissions against the judging criteria, before the deadline, so you can still act on what you hear. Submit early to the Devpost Discord's Build with AI Basics forum if you want yours in the mix. Stuck? Ask in Discord or come to Cup of Joe office hours (Tuesdays Oct 6 and Oct 13 , 3:00 pm ET, Discord voice). Setup help and all event details are on the Resources tab. What to build A new app, built with the Devpost Learn Skill Pack. The skills will help you find an idea if you don't have one, and cut it down if you have too much of one. Three requirements, all checked at submission: New project, started from an empty folder during the submission period. Old ideas are fine, old code is not. Built with the skills. Run them in your coding agent. Planning docs in the repo. Your public repository must include the scope.md, prd.md, and spec.md files the skills generate.

title: Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026
description: THE META VR START DEVELOPER COMPETITION IS BACK! This year’s eight-week challenge calls on Start program members to build the next generation of Entertainment, Gaming, and Productivity experiences for Meta VR devices – including Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest. We’re looking for hands-first apps that make interaction more natural and gameplay more intuitive than ever before. Last year, over 2,900 developers joined the competition and delivered more than 650 submissions that pushed the boundaries of immersive technology. This year, we’re raising the bar again. Whether you’re a first-time Start developer with a breakthrough idea or a seasoned creator ready to showcase what’s possible with the latest platform capabilities, this is your moment to help redefine the future of VR. Here’s what’s waiting for you: 🤝 Build hands-first. Design experiences powered by hand interactions that feel natural, responsive, and deeply immersive—no controllers required. 🛠️ Explore new tech. Take advantage of the latest OS capabilities and device features across Meta VR Glasses and Meta Quest, accelerate your development with AI tooling, including Meta VR CLI. 🌍 Join a global community. Boost your skills through mentor programming, collaborate with fellow developers, share insights, and learn from a thriving network of experienced VR developers. 🏆 Compete for $1M in cash prizes with top prizes of $100,000. The future of VR is in your hands literally . We can’t wait to see what you build. GETTING STARTED If you’re not already a member of the Start program, apply now to join the competition. Estimated time: 5 minutes Explore last year’s winning submissions and Sample Use Cases for Inspiration Estimated time: 30 minutes Entertainment Gaming I ​​Quest Gamer Segments Productivity: AnExplorer Hands: Hands Physics Lab I ​​ Table Troopers Follow a Quickstart Tutorial (below) Estimated time: 30 minutes Unity: VR 101 I VR 102 Unreal: How to Make VR Games in UE5 Android: From Mobile to VR Overview Immersive Web SDK: Your First Steps into Immersive Web Development Getting Started with Hands & Eyes Check out the Resources tab for more technical documentation and visit the Meta Developer Forum for ongoing support and access to upcoming competition events and workshops.

title: Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026
description: About the challenge Welcome to the Multimodal AI Hackathon 2026, organized by KamandPrompt, the Programming Club of IIT Mandi, Augli.ai, PurpleRain Tech, and LDV Labs. This nationwide hackathon invites students to work at the intersection of Generative AI, Agentic AI, and real-world problem-solving, applying these emerging technologies to domains where they can create genuine impact. Multimodal AI systems, ones that can reason across text, images, data, and more, are increasingly capable of tackling problems that were previously out of reach for automated systems. Yet in fields like Space research, BioTech, and Education, this potential remains largely untapped. Building solutions in these domains requires not just technical skill but a genuine understanding of the problems being solved, which is exactly the gap this hackathon is designed to close. This hackathon offers participants the opportunity to design and build solutions that could meaningfully improve how problems are approached in Space, BioTech, and Education. Whether it's a tool that accelerates research, an application that improves access to learning, or a system that solves an overlooked operational bottleneck, your work here has the potential to extend well beyond a submission page. Get started - Mode: Fully online, nationwide - Team Size: Solo/Upto 4 members (inter-college teams allowed) - Duration: 15 days - Tracks: 4 tracks across Space, BioTech, and Education - Registration: Free, no fees - Submissions to be made on devpost - All further information will be shared in the official Discord community post-registration Please note that this hackathon have a well defined set of Problem Statements and Judging criteria and the submissions will be evaluated on the same basis Problem statements: click here Join Discord community: https://discord.gg/UD8EVcdcq

title: AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS) Agentic AI Partner Hackathon
description: Calling all AWS Partners! We are inviting you to build the next wave of conversational solutions on AWS Communication Developer Services (CDS)! AWS CDS enables AWS Partners to help customers engage users at a global scale through AWS End User Messaging (EUM) which includes Rich Communication Services (RCS), Short Message Services (SMS), and WhatsApp. It also includes Amazon Simple Email Service (SES). AWS CDS is the infrastructure that powers messaging across Amazon.com , Amazon Cognito, SNS, and Amazon Connect. AWS CDS is often used for one-time passwords (OTP), notifications, and rules-based chatbots that follow rigid scripts. We challenge you to think beyond this. The future of customer engagement is conversational: reaching customers in the channel (i.e. email vs. RCS vs. WhatsApp) they prefer, picking up right where the last conversation left off, and using two-way communication so customers tell you directly what they want and share signals that improve your products and services. Picture omnichannel experiences where a conversation starts in one channel and completes an action in another: a prescription refill reminder via SMS that lets the patient find and schedule the nearest pharmacy pickup through RCS with a tap, then sends dosage instructions via email, all without leaving the messaging experience. Push the boundaries. Build agentic solutions where AWS CDS is the communications backbone, powered by AI such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Surprise us with your real customer and industry solutions! Why You Should Participate Innovate with AWS CDS . Get hands-on with AWS CDS combined with agentic AI powered by Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Solve Real Customer Problems . Create agentic solutions tied to customer and industry use cases that can scale across your customer base. Package your hackathon submission into a repeatable offering, list it on AWS Marketplace, and win AWS Specialist GTM and enablement support to accelerate real customer deals. Win Big . Compete for your share of $40,000 USD in cash prizes, in addition to an opportunity for a joint case study and 1:1 access to AWS Specialists to build and grow your AWS CDS practice and hackathon solution. Visibility for Your Organization . Winners will be announced via Devpost and the top winner will be offered a joint case study with AWS. Drive awareness and new leads to your practice. Direct Access to AWS Specialists . Join live webinars and weekly office hours to ask questions, get feedback, and shape the services roadmap. How to Get Started Now Brainstorm Your Idea . Think outside the box to improve customer communication experience through AWS CDS. Review the Tech Stack . Familiarize yourself with the AWS CDS services and how to pair them with agentic AI frameworks such as Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. See the Requirements below. Form Your Team (Optional). Find collaborators within the same AWS Partner organization who are excited to improve customer problems through AWS CDS. Diverse skillsets in development, architecture, and customer engagement can go a long way. Start Building . Stand up an RCS agent within 5 minutes to develop an entire solution, decide later to use RCS or phone numbers for each country you’re serving, and expand from there.

title: WarriorHacks 2.0
description: Who Are We? Westwood Computer Science Club is located at Westwood High School in Austin, Texas. We've won the Spike App Prediction Competition hosted by Harvard students and generated millions of views on our Instagram reels and posts. Hackathon Tracks This hackathon is split into two tracks: hackathon and ideathon. Participants who select the hackathon track are required to submit a project involving code related to the hackathon theme. Participants who select the ideathon track are not required to submit a project involving code. Instead, you will be tasked with conceptually developing a solution to the given theme. Theme Create a project that solves an issue in your community, county, state, or nation. Quick Links WarriorHacks 2.0 Site Westwood CS Club Discord Westwood CS Club Instagram
